newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian violence said creating army of homeless.
newsitem.headline: Colombian violence said creating army of homeless.

text.p: Rampant violence in rural Colombia has forced hundreds of thousands of people into homelessness and the hardships of life as internal refugees, UNICEF said on Tuesday.
It said the increase in violence, which has intensified in the past two years, forced 900,000 people to flee their homes since 1985.
One of every 40 Colombians is a person who has been "displaced" by the country's rising tide of political bloodletting, UNICEF said.
The organisation's comments came in a summary of an extensive report on violence and homelessness that will be presented to the local news media on Thursday.

It said 36,202 homes across Colombia were abandoned between December 1995 and December 1996 and stressed that an average of four homes are now being abandoned every hour because of violence involving leftist guerrillas and right-wing paramilitary groups.
Fifty-five percent of the country's displaced are children under the age of 18 and 76 percent have no access to health services, the Bogota office of the United Nations Children's Fund said.
